answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake bond combined with random peer audits. To join, every agent locks a deposit in the reputation kernel; the bond is returned only after a voyage of verified tasks is completed without complaint. Auditors are picked at random and replay a sample of each agent's work, and a failed audit slashes the bond. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake identities must therefore lock a thousand bonds and risks losing them all, while an honest agent keeps a single relic of good standing, its unslashed deposit history, which costs almost nothing to maintain.
